notes.subject: car
notes.text: Large white pickup, often partly visible, with an antenna on the front. The Panamanian truck is nearly always fully blurred.

notes.subject: plate
notes.text: Short white plates with blue text, giving a light blue tint when blurred.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Stop signs read ALTO, in a thinner font than the Panamanian ones.

notes.subject: car
notes.text: Red taxis carry yellow triangles with the town name and a province letter.

notes.subject: bollard
notes.text: The bollard equivalent is a vertical orange board with three black circles.

notes.subject: pole
notes.text: Long silver insulators are standard.

notes.subject: pole
notes.text: Common pole top: a low crossbar with one insulator on one side and two on the other, usually with support bars.

notes.subject: pole
notes.text: A single insulator attached to the side near the top of the pole is common.

notes.subject: pole
notes.text: Pole-mounted lamps have a blue dot on top.

notes.subject: pole
notes.text: Thin metal crossbar bent 90 degrees into an L shape is common.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Many signs, especially diamond warning signs, have a cross on the back.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: Round electricity meters, often with a large metal box beside them.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: Ads for a beer with a black eagle mascot are a common sight.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Lush and tropical: rolling hills, farmland lowlands, a chain of volcanoes down the middle and patches of rainforest.

notes.subject: architecture
notes.text: Pastel concrete houses with dark red metal or plastic-tile roofs, low or boxy, heavily fenced with barred windows.

notes.subject: pole
notes.text: White pole plates with black lettering are specific to the greater capital area.

notes.subject: pole
notes.text: Pole tops with one insulator on one side and two on the other are found in and around the capital.

notes.subject: pole
notes.text: Pole attachments made of numbers shaped from wire are found in central Alajuela and over the border in Heredia.

notes.subject: pole
notes.text: Tall, three-section yellow pole paint with numbers is mainly in Puntarenas and southern Alajuela.

notes.subject: pole
notes.text: Shorter yellow pole paint with all numbers undivided is mainly in Guanacaste and northwest Alajuela.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Most banana plantations are in the Caribbean province of Limón.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Flat Caribbean lowlands with farmland, grey dirt, straight roads and often overcast skies.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Most oil palm plantations are along the Pacific coast in Puntarenas.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Rice fields are mostly south of Bagaces in Guanacaste, with raised edges around the paddies.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Most coffee plantations lie in the central valley.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: Fences made of irregular wooden branches or logs are most common in the west.

notes.subject: architecture
notes.text: Houses on stilts are mostly found on the northeast coast.

notes.subject: bollard
notes.text: Yellow bollards sit between the centre lines on Route 32 from near the capital to the Caribbean coast.
